title: Expose browser login and invitation acceptance transport
verify: A bound Telegram or Google identity can complete the browser/API login path and receives the existing foundation_session cookie as HttpOnly, Path=/, SameSite=Lax; Secure is set for HTTPS and relaxed/omitted for local HTTP development, the user reaches the permitted context, and access is rejected after logout or revocation.

An issued invitation remains bound to server-issued authentication state through start and callback; either provider can complete a valid callback for the exact bound account/session, while tampered or forged/mismatched callback state is rejected without consuming the still-valid invitation, and expired, revoked, reused, duplicate, and failed callbacks return safe errors without partial state.
Routes, hooks, form actions, and SSR loads contain no direct database write, client-trusted role/center authorization, or provider secret exposure.

evidence: The honest initial focused RED could not import the absent browser transport module; the later Attempt 1 focused gate failed 3/4 tests because issue() dropped invitationToken, so valid and rollback callbacks lost invitation context and wrong-account handling took the incorrect redirect path.
This failure remains correction history only; no lifecycle or scheduler state changed and no executor receipt was promoted to independent proof.

Independent disposable browser/API probe passed 3 tests for Telegram/Google login, exact HTTPS/local-HTTP foundation_session cookie options, actor resolution, logout/revocation, invitation acceptance/replay/rejection, and rollback; live SSR/HTTP smoke and required check/build/full-test/diff gates also passed.
Attempt 2 corrected only server-owned invitation-state continuity; the current report records VERDICT: PASS without changing task scope or lifecycle.
Independent T3 adversarial review found no material ownership, state/replay, cookie, SSR, privacy, secret-leakage, or direct-persistence finding across the browser/API transport.
The current semantic artifact records SEMANTIC_VERDICT: semantic-pass; task identity/status, dependency, lifecycle, and retry budget remain unchanged.

purpose: Turn the existing provider/session boundaries into the minimum real SvelteKit login, logout, and invitation browser/API flow.
success_outcome: A user can login with either accepted provider or accept a valid invitation through SvelteKit, receive a secure server session, reach the permitted context, and receive safe denial/error behavior for invalid or revoked state.
anti_goals: Do not implement provider verification or persistence in routes; consume TASK-019 public boundaries.
Do not trust query/form role, center, account, or invitation ownership for authorization.
Do not add a password, role-selection, or unauthenticated development login path.

stop_conditions: Stop if the HTTP flow needs a new module, direct table access, a second database/store, or a change to the provider/session contract.

constraints: Routes/hooks/UI are thin adapters and all protected operations recheck server-side actor/session state.
The existing foundation_session cookie remains the single session cookie for this local MVP.
HTTP/SSR tests use disposable fixtures and injected adapters; live provider credentials are not embedded in tests.
invariants: Invalid, absent, or revoked sessions cannot reach protected operations.
Invitation callback never accepts a client-selected role, center, or account.
Invitation capability remains bound to server-issued authentication state; tampered or forged callback state is rejected without consuming a still-valid invitation.
A failed callback or rejected invitation leaves account, membership, invitation, identity, and session state unchanged.
